Abstract 10 
A key question in origins-of-life research, is whether heritability, and thus evolution, 11 
could have preceded genes. Out-of-equilibrium chemical reaction networks with multiple 12 
autocatalytic motifs may provide chemical “memory” and serve as units of heritability, but 13 
experimental validation is lacking. We established conditions that may be conducive to the 14 
emergence of heritable variation and developed methods to search for heritability and 15 
autocatalysis. We prepared a food set (FS) of three organic species, three inorganic salts and 16 
pyrite. We conducted a serial dilution experiment where FS was incubated for 24 hours, after 17 
which a 20% fraction was transferred into freshly prepared FS that went through the same 18 
procedure, repeated for 10 generations. To serve as controls, we also incubated the fresh 19 
solutions in each generation. We compared the chemical composition of transfer vials and no-20 
transfer controls using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LCMS), with metrics adapted 21
